items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: in the family we have my nephew, which is my sister Rose, who passed away a couple of years ago. Her son Danny Barker, and everybody says he's pretty good guitar and banjures.

ctx.x: And Louie's a couple of years younger than you or so?

Yeah, I was a couple of years younger than me, just about a couple of years. And then we have, in the family we have my nephew, which is my sister Rose, who passed away a couple of years ago. Her son Danny Barker, and everybody says he's pretty good guitar and banjures. Played with all the named bands around New York. He's still in New York. He's trying to get his book together. Which I hope he does. Because I'm tired of hearing about that book.
That'll be a good one now when he gets it.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And he was beautiful in doing that, because he helped me all through my career.

ctx.x: Well, he was my godfather. They always do that, see, if you're a little youngster whose (?) is not capable of taking care of a baby, an infant... You know, nine years...he'd be nine years older than the infant, and you could help him or sponsor him, christen him, take care of him if something happened to the parent. That is the procedure of the godparent. And he is my godparent.
And he was beautiful in doing that, because he helped me all through my career.

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: So, I got a letter from my uncle Paul and I told him what had happened. He said, I'll send you a banjo.

ctx.x: Who did Lloyd Arthur Dog play with?

He played with the Arnold Brass Band. They played first clarinet. He died young with a social disease. My great-aunt term. He was a shy boy. He was a basketball sergeant. Some sportswoman enticed him and got in a corral and contacted his disease. And they wouldn't tell the old folks that he was sick. And somehow they detected that he had this trouble. And when they found out about it and rushed him to the hospital, it was too late. So he died of this sickness. And this is just a lot on the planet. So Michael Paul…
Back to Florida for a minute. What were the bands like in Florida other than the band you were with?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Paul told him, “If you hire somebody else, I quit. Hire my nephew.” So he hired me.

ctx.x: How did you first get in Cab’s band?

I’m around there, and I’m starting from the bottom. It’s 1930, with Harry White’s band. I’m with Dave Nelson’s band. I’m with Danny Logan’s band. I’m with Luis Russell’s band. Played with Louis . . . played a short tour with Louis Armstrong, through Virginia. Bill Johnson got drunk, and Luis Russell wanted to hire somebody else. Paul told him, “If you hire somebody else, I quit. Hire my nephew.” So he hired me. Bill Johnson got well again and then Bill Johnson got drunk again. They had to tolerate Bill. Bill…
This is not the same Bill Johnson that played with King Oliver.
